chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Muthannā, from Zurārah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAjlān, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for the near relatives.
He said: They are the Imams عليهم السلام.

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams عليهم السلام as the intended referents in this explanation
key_terms.الْقُرْبَى: the near relatives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.قَوْلِهِ: His statement, referring to the divine speech in the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Who are meant by “the near relatives” in Qur'an 42:23 according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about affection for the near relatives as referring to the Imams عليهم السلام. It presents the Qur'anic command of mawaddah toward the قربى as an indication of their religious authority and special rank.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Musna, from Zurara, from Abdullah Bin Ajlan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of the Exalted
[42:23] Say: I do not ask of you any Recompense for it except for the cordiality for my near relatives.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Asha‘ari from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from al-Muthanna from Zurara from ‘Abdallah ibn al-‘Ajlan from abu Ja‘far (a.s.)
about the words of Allah, the most High.
“(Muhammad), say, “I do not ask you for any payment for my preaching to you except (your) love of(my near) relatives.. .” [42:23].
The Imam (a.s.) said, “They (the relatives) are the Imams.”
